newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold seen capped at $323 resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold seen capped at $323 resistance.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold may drift slightly higher, but is unlikely to break through resistance around $323 an ounce and may see further downside tests, dealers and analysts said on Monday.
Silver is vulnerable to probes lower after failing to break $4.40 resistance, they added.
GOLD -
The market was moving out of its oversold region and might have difficulty confronting resistance. The 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI) was at 29 at Friday's close, off a low of 16 hit on July 7.
The ceiling around $323 was based on previous highs of $323.25 on July 7, $322.50 on July 8 and $322.10 on Friday. The 10-day moving average at $324.44 would also weigh on prices.
"With the technical indicators drifting sideways, gold's current period of consolidation looks vulnerable to further downside tests," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
Many in the market believed gold would eventually bottom out around $310 or $308, another analyst in continental Europe said.
Nearby support was pegged around $317/18, with the next floor around $315, followed by last week's 12-year lows of $313.60.

The market must be wary of when large speculators will cover their short positions, which total 80,000 lots on Comex, he added. A big drop in the U.S. stock market might prove an impetus to buy, but at the moment they saw no reason to do so.
At 0800 GMT spot gold was quoted at $321.70/322.10, up 60 cents from Friday's New York close.
SILVER -
Prices were shaky after failing to break above the $4.40 per ounce mark three times -- on Friday, Thursday and on July 8.
Nearby support was pegged at $4.30 with $4.25 the next floor.

"With the technical indicators remaining weak, the precious metal remains vulnerable to further downside tests...we favour tests of $4.30 and below," Squires said, referring to the Comex September contract.
Like gold, silver was moving out of an oversold condition, with the 14-day RSI rising to 32 from a low of 23 hit on July 7.
At 0815 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.37/4.39, up one cent from Friday's New York close.
PLATINUM -
The market was backing off from $410 nearby resistance, with long speculative positions hanging over the market.
The 10-day moving average at $411 would also be an obstacle.

Prices had recovered from lows around $395 on perceptions that Russian deliveries were not seen as enough to satisfy the market, but supplies from long hedge funds were seen impeding any rally, an analyst said.
If prices broke through $410, next resistance was pegged at $420, around the July 7 peak.
At 0815 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $407.00/411.00, up $9.00 from Friday's New York close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
